Subject: Tenant isolation enablement — readiness playlist & gating asks

Hi Liam / Tempora infra team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Private. To keep the activation window tight, I put together a short "playlist" of the isolation and egress items we need signed off before we schedule Day 0. This focuses on the tenancy segregation, KMS access, and egress gating you asked about.

Top asks (short):
- Confirm dedicated tenant VPC CIDR and whether there is overlapping addressing with Tempora corp (we need a /24 minimum).
- Provide the list of service accounts that will require cross-account KMS decrypt (CSV attached sample).
- Approve the egress allowlist (port level) and whether a NAT gateway or proxy will be used.
- Confirm bastion/jumpbox IP allowlist for Day 0 engineer access (one public IP range preferred).
- Delivery of a network diagram (reference attached template).

I attached the segmentation diagram template and a sample tenant IAM CSV. Ben/ Karthik/ Naomi — please add any gating items we should surface to Tempora (I tried to keep it laser-focused).

Goal: sign-off on these items by EOD Wed (23 July) so we can lock in an activation date the week of 28th.

Thanks,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — useful checklist. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) CIDR: we can spare a /24 (10.47.100.0/24) but need to confirm there are no overlapping VPN routes; our SRE will validate.
2) KMS: we run a centrally managed KMS in GCP; can you confirm the exact key policy fields Redwood needs? We prefer to keep key admin scoped to our cloud team.
3) Egress: we will route egress through an existing proxy cluster — port 443 only. Does Redwood require NAT IPs for token callbacks or can we accept proxy-based egress?

We'll populate the attached CSV with service accounts and upload the diagram by tomorrow noon.

— Liam

Liam — quick answers inline:

- Overlapping routes: if you have a VPN that could conflict we'll need the ASN and route prefixes so our network team can validate.
- KMS: Redwood's private deployment needs an encrypted key to unwrap the model KV cache and any customer-managed secrets. We support both cross-project key grants and customer-provided CMKs. For Tempora's central KMS we usually ask for a decrypt grant on a key ARN-equivalent and a service account that Redwood will use. Karthik, please add the exact policy snippet.
- Egress: proxy-only egress is fine; we only require outbound connectivity to our control plane endpoints for telemetry and fallback. If you do proxy-only, please add the control-plane FQDNs to the proxy allowlist (I'll add links).

Also, for Day 0 we ask for a test VM that can reach the tenant VPC CIDR so our engineers can validate routing and NAT behavior. A small temporary instance is enough.

Ben Carter
Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Liam — adding the KMS policy snippet and control-plane endpoints here.

Policy snippet (example fields for Tempora KMS grant):
- Principal: service-account@redwood-prod
- Actions: cloudkms.cryptoDecrpyt, cloudkms.cryptoDecrypt (provider-specific names; sample attached as tenant-iam-sample.csv)
- Conditions: request is restricted to tenant VPC CIDR 

Control-plane FQDNs to allow out:
- controlplane.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- fallback-cache.redwood.ai

If proxy-only egress: ensure those FQDNs resolve via your proxy and TLS interception is disabled for those hosts (we validate certificate pinning in the agent).

I'll also attach a small checklist for Day 0:
- Temporary test VM in tenant VPC with public IP for engineer SSH access (add to allowlist)
- KMS grant for the Redwood service account
- Egress allowlist updated with control-plane FQDNs
- Upload network diagram to the Drive folder (link below)
